chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed by a veiled woman who was in Ihram, so he said: 'Enter into Ihram, uncover your face, and let down your garment from the top of your head, for if you were to veil (your face), your complexion would not change.' A man asked: 'To where should she let it down?' He said: 'To cover her eyes.' I said: 'Does it reach her mouth?' He said: 'Yes.'
And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The female in Ihram should not wear jewelry, nor dyed clothes, except if it is dyed with a dye that does not fade (or return to its original state).'

key_terms.لَا يَرْدَعُ: Does not fade/return to original state
key_terms.لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ لَوْنُكِ: Your complexion/color would not change (implying the veil does not alter the natural look)
key_terms.مُتَنَقِّبَةٍ: A woman wearing a face veil (naqab)
key_terms.مُحْرِمَةٌ: A woman in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a woman's clothing and face covering when she is in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Hammad ibn Uthman, clarifies the distinction between the full face veil (niqab) and the permissible head covering (qarqan) for women in Ihram, emphasizing that the face remains visible while the eyes are covered. The hadith further specifies that jewelry is prohibited and that dyed garments are only allowed if the dye is permanent (not 'rad'), reflecting the Shia juristic focus on the material properties of clothing during the sacred state. This ruling underscores the balance between modesty and the specific restrictions of Ihram, distinguishing it from general hijab requirements.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Abu Ja’farasws passed by a veiled woman (in Naqaab) and she was in Ihraam. So heasws said: ‘Wear Ihraam, and uncover your face, and relax your cloth from the top of your head, for if you were to veil (Naqaab), your colour would not change’. So a man asked, ‘Up to where should she relax it?’ So heasws said: ‘To uncover her eyes’. I said, ‘It should not reach her mouth?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
And Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The female in Ihraam should not wear an ornament, nor dyed clothes except if it is dyed and cannot be returned (to its original state)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to a woman veiled in the state of Ihram, ‘Assume the state of Ihram with your face uncovered and allow your clothes to hang down from over your head; if you use veil, your color will not change.’ A man then asked, ‘How far down must she hang her clothes? Must she cover her eyes?’ I then asked, ‘Can it reach down to her mouth?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is permissible.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘Women in the state of Ihram must not wear jewelry and dyed clothes, unless it (dye) is of saffron.’”
